title: Beni Mellal city and foothills, 21 Aug to 2 Sep 2026
summary: From 21 Aug to 2 Sep 2026 the radar shows 0.76 km2 turning brighter in HV around Beni Mellal, against 0.29 km2 darker. Most of the brighter area, 0.52 km2, is on the changing fields.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: In 12 days mean HV moved by -0.02 dB and mean HH by 0.03 dB. In HV, 0.76 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.29 km2 darker; in HH, 0.77 km2 turned brighter and 0.32 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields rose 0.68 dB in HV on average, with 0.52 km2 brighter and only 0.05 km2 darker. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 0.11 km2 brighter and 0.09 km2 darker. Built-up land fell 0.26 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the brighter fields: new crops coming up in late August, which add plants that scatter HV; a field visit would confirm it. Possible cause for the small changes on built-up land: speckle or viewing differences; stable targets on more dates would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow. Small patches are close to what speckle alone can produce at the 3 dB threshold.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: A farm office could check which plots were sown in late August. Follow the brighter fields on the next dates to see the crop grow.
